Welcome to Aspen
Aspen Special Educational Needs Unit
Aspen is Shepherdswell Academy’s Special Educational Needs (SEN) Unit for students with Social Communication and Interaction needs, including many learners with an Autism diagnosis. We support children who find communication challenging. However, Aspen is not able to support children with severe or profound SEMH presentations. Where appropriate, we aim to support students to access mainstream classes, either for part of the day or specific subjects. Most of our pupils are learning through the pre National Curriculum and the National Curriculum, carefully adapted to meet individual needs.
Aspen Classes and Pathways
Aspen supports students across three mixed year classes (Years 3–6). Each class follows a different learning pathway, matched to students’ developmental, sensory and communication needs.

Dragonflies Wraparound Care
Dragonflies Breakfast Club operates from 7.30 – 8.35am.
Dragonflies After School Club operates from the end of the school day until 6:00pm and is located at Orchard Academy. Pupils at Shepherdswell Academy are transported by either the school mini-bus or a walking bus to Orchard Academy
Our wraparound care is a welcoming and friendly environment for all children at Shepherdswell Academy. Children are given choices to participate in a variety of arts and crafts, sports, team games, or simply just relax and read a book in the quiet area.
During Dragonflies Breakfast Club, children are provided with breakfast and at Dragonflies After School sessions, children will be provided with a light snack. All menus for food at our extended care is carefully planned and adapted to any dietary requirements.
Booking is available allowing you to select the days you require. Once a booking has been confirmed the place is secure unless cancelled. Bookings and payments need to be made in advance for all sessions that are required, through Arbor, to ensure a place for your child/ren.
Please note that we predict that our extended care will be very popular and advise that you book your sessions in advance.
Please be aware that no food will be served after 8:20 am. We do not accept entry from any child using Dragonflies breakfast club after 8:30am
Costs
Dragonflies Breakfast Club £3.00 per session per child
Dragonflies After School Club 3:15pm – 6:00pm £8.50 per session per child
Dragonflies Wraparound Care is currently unavailable for pupils aged under 3 due to adult ratios.

Nursery Curriculum
We are so excited to welcome you to our nursery at Shepherdswell Academy.
Our Nursery class is called Otters and caters for children aged 3 and 4. The teacher is Mrs Smith.
The curriculum
We follow the Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum. This has seven areas of learning split into three prime areas which are Communication and Language, Personal, Social and Emotional Development, and Physical Development and four specific areas which are Mathematics, Literacy, Expressive Arts and Design, and Understanding the World.
Each term we have a topic or theme that we focus our learning around. This term our topic is: all about me!
Please see the curriculum overview for more information on this.
We really value everything you do at home to support your child and love to hear about their achievements at home. We will send out ‘WOW moment’ slips for you to note down any of your child’s accomplishments to send back into school. We will share these with the class during circle time and add to your child’s learning journal.
Reading books
We really value reading in Nursery so your child will be part of storytime every session they are with us. Reading for pleasure is so important to develop your child’s interest in stories as well as introducing them to new vocabulary and concepts such as rhyming. We have a well-stocked reading area in our classroom and the children will have opportunities to visit our school library over the year. Once the children are settled, they will have the opportunity to borrow a book each week from the school library / classroom. This will be a book chosen by your child and will reflect their interests. We will change books once per week, we will be unable to give your child a new book until the borrowed one is returned.
We encourage you to share stories each day with your child and support them to learn book skills such as holding the book in the correct way and carefully turning the pages. Talking about the story and pictures will help their understanding and build a good foundation for enjoying books.
Toileting
We encourage our Nursery children to be as independent as possible when using the toilet but will offer support when needed. Please support your child to recognise when they need the toilet and to ask to go. We will work alongside you to support your child with any toileting needs to develop their independence in this area.
General
Please ensure that your child has their named book bag and named water bottle (water only) in school every day and that your child’s uniform is also named. Please check your child’s book bag each day, as letters are often sent this way. The children are provided with a healthy fruit or vegetable snack during their session. You are welcome to pack your own snack, but it must be fruit or vegetables and this can include dried fruit. During snack time we encourage the children to pour their own water from a jug into a cup to help develop their independence and hand-eye co-ordination. We also develop our speaking and listening skills during this time by talking with each other around the table.
If you have any questions, please talk to Mrs Hampson or contact the school office.
We are looking forward to a fantastic year!

Reception Curriculum
Welcome to Reception
We have one class in Reception this year. The class will be Hedgehogs class with Miss Weatherspoon.
The curriculum
Each term we have a topic or theme that we focus our learning around.
This term our topic is: all about me.
We follow the Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum. This has seven areas of learning, three prime areas which are Communication and Language, Personal, Social and Emotional Development, and Physical Development. The four specific areas are Mathematics, Literacy, Expressive Arts and Design, and Understanding the World.
Reading books
This year we have a big focus on reading, your child will have a daily phonics lesson and reading for pleasure session as well as reading with adults 1:1. We expect your child to read at home at least 3 times a week for a minimum of ten minutes. Your children will be getting two different types of reading books. One book will be a RWI book that is matched to their phonics/reading ability. At the beginning of the year this will be a wordless book for your child to discuss the pictures, beginning to answer questions and create their own narrative around the pictures. It is also to learn book skills such as turning the pages and holding the book the in the correct way. The other type of book is a library book used for reading for pleasure, your child might not be able to read this book alone, but it is a great book to share together or even make up different stories using the pictures. Your child will choose this book from the school library or class book box. Book change days are Monday and Thursdays.
Reading at home with your child is extremely important and you should aim to listen to your child read and record this in their reading record. Please ensure your child’s reading book, reading for pleasure book and reading record are in their book bag everyday as we will also aim to read with them 1-1 throughout the week whilst they are at school If you do not bring back your child’s reading book, we will be unable to change this for you.
PE
PE days will be Monday.
In Reception children have PE once a week. During our independent learning sessions, we have access to our outside garden area which has space for children to run and develop their gross motor skills.
On Mondays your child should come to school in the correct PE kit. PE can take place both inside and outside, so make sure they are dressed appropriately for the weather. Children should have long hair tied up and no earrings on PE days.
Homework
We will have a half termly Homework Pick n Mix. This will be sent out every half term. Children are given a homework book where you can record their homework. Homework is about giving the children the opportunity to develop their learning, and to give you a chance to learn together as a family. Your child might like to draw or write in the book, or you might like to write for them and write what they have told you. At the beginning of the year, you might need to write for your child, however we encourage the children to try and have ago themselves. If they cannot write, try to encourage them to draw a picture.
General
Please ensure that your child has their named book bag and named water bottle (water only) in school every day and that your child’s uniform is also named. Please check your child’s book bag each day, as letters are often sent this way. The children are provided with a healthy fruit or vegetable snack each morning, they are also given a carton of milk. Milk is provided by the Government. Until they turn 5, If you would like your child to continue receiving milk after they are 5, please arrange payment with the office.
If you have any questions, please talk to Miss Weatherspoon or contact the school office.
We are looking forward to a fantastic year!

SEND and Inclusion
Shepherdswell Academy's SENCO is Luke Allwood and he can be contacted via Telephone: 01908 735865 or email: SEND@shepherdswell.emat.uk.
Milton Keynes Council's SEND Local Offer can be accessed by clicking on the link below, alternatively you can read more about Shepherdswell Academy's inclusion practices and equality objectives by clicking on the tabs below.
At Shepherdswell Academy Every Child Matters. We believe that the most important function of the school is to maintain an environment in which every member of the school is able to achieve success and self fulfilment. There must be a total consistency of expectation that everyone (irrespective of gender, race, sexual orientation or culture) should feel safe and secure, have empathy for all others, and place a high value upon individual achievement and personal development.
We are highly committed to promoting equality and inclusion within the school and local community. We actively promote and value the individuality of all of our children. We are committed to giving every one of our children maximum opportunity to achieve the highest of standards. We do this by taking account of pupils’ varied life experiences and needs. We believe that all children have an entitlement to a broad and balanced academic and social curriculum, which is accessible to them, and to be fully included in all aspects of school life and we have very high expectations for all children. The achievements, attitudes and well-being of all our children are central to all we say and do. We believe that all children should be equally valued in school. We will strive to eliminate prejudice and discrimination, and to develop an environment where all children can flourish and feel safe. We aim to engender a strong sense of community and belonging, and to offer new opportunities to learners who may have experienced previous difficulties.
Shepherdswell Academy is passionate about and totally committed to inclusion and believes learners are partners in the learning process. We believe that educational inclusion is about equal opportunities for all learners, whatever their age, gender, ethnicity, impairment, attainment and background. Thus we value and provide for our learners in the best way as to meet their needs and respond appropriately according to their varied life experiences and needs.
Our school is committed to being a fully inclusive school. We therefore actively seek to remove the barriers to learning and participation that can hinder or exclude individual pupils, or groups of pupils. This means that equality of opportunity is a right and reality for our children.

Local Advisory Board
The Orchard and Shepherdswell Local Advisory Board is the local tier of governance of East Midlands Academy Trust, and it acts as a sub-committee to the Trust Board. Members of the Local Advisory Board as known as Governors.
The key roles of the LAB are:
These roles translate specifically into the following tasks:
The LAB’s role is not to manage the Academy as such. This is done through the Board of Trustees. Therefore, the LAB is not required to take decisions on staff or financial matters affecting the Academy.
Governors at the LAB will gain an understanding of strategic issues that impact on the Academy and will be updated on them regularly by the Headteacher, but they are not required to have direct responsibility for them. Instead the LAB should be in a position to assess the impact of the Academy locally; how it is contributing to the local community, how it is relating to local families and how it understands local issues. This in turn, will enable the LAB to contribute effectively to decisions which may require LAB involvement.
The LAB is drawn from the staff of the school, parents and the wider community that the school serves. The usual term of office for a governor is four years but many members of the LAB stand for re-election and serve more than one term. Members of a LAB need to take a full and active role in fulfilling the role assigned to them by the Board. This will include regular visits to the Academy and attending up to six meetings per year.
To contact any of our governors, please email governance@emat.uk

Meet Our Governors
Chris is an experienced business leader and human resources professional with extensive experience in banking, project management and human resources, specialising in business transformation, M&A, employee experience and leadership development. He is a Chartered member of the CIPD and an alumnus of the University of Sunderland Business School. He enjoys supporting young people with access to early careers as a mentor for the Social Mobility Foundation.
Chris is a parent governor with two children at Orchard and is looking forward to bringing insights and experience to support Orchard & Shepherdswell values and maintain high standards
Kirsty is an Early Years specialist teacher and has been working within the sector including KS1 for over a decade. During this time, she has been a both a team leader and manager of an Early Years setting where she enjoys teaching young children and instils valuable hands on learning experiences. This helps the children make sense of the world around them - thus building strong key foundations as they begin their educational journey.
She has an Early Years teacher qualification (EYTS) and is very much looking forward to obtaining her Qualified Teacher Status (QTS) this year.
Having previously run a pre-school which was charity owned and part of the committee she ensured the smooth running of the Early Years setting. She is also a member of a local carnival committee who are dedicated all year round to organise and co-ordinate a fun packed family weekend out every summer.
Kirsty is currently a Reception teacher at Shepherdswell Academy and joined in August 2022. She is also part of the school PTA.
Graham is a Programme Director / Consultant currently working in an international military environment specialising in communications, intelligence and cyber projects. He has an extensive background in telecoms and electronics spanning various business sectors. Graham is an associate of the BCS and holds PRINCE2 and MSP Practitioner and APMP qualifications. Away from work, Graham is married with 3 children, so a lot of his time is spent driving and supporting them at ballet and gymnastics lessons. When he does get the time, he likes classic cars and running.
Ross is an experienced and dynamic professional whose career spans senior leadership, digital transformation, and operations across both private and public-sector environments. Ross brings to the school a strong grasp of complex organisational frameworks, stakeholder engagement and innovative change management, enriched by his experience at board-level and international business contexts. Ross has experience in employment tribunals and high court proceedings involving complex shareholder matters, and has recently transitioned his business into employee ownership by way of an Employee Ownership Trust.
He holds a Certificate in Company Direction from the Institute of Directors (IoD), underscoring his commitment to governance, strategic decision-making and ethical leadership.
Ross is new to school governance and is looking forward to making a positive impact.
Outside his professional life, Ross is a devoted father to two young daughters. He is a passionate supporter of Northampton Saints, enjoys playing the guitar and has a long-standing love of quizzing—having participated in the Milton Keynes Quiz League from 1996 through to 2024.
Hitesh is a Qualified Chartered Certified Accountant and a seasoned Chief Financial Officer with a strong background in business transformation, financial planning, and private equity engagements. He has successfully led multiple business turnarounds, including the trade sale of a high-end luxury product business recently. He has worked in including manufacturing/marine /automotive /retail/food.
Having held multiple Board positions, including being Chairman of Radical Sportscars he brings a wealth of commercial knowledge to complement his role as Governor for the EMAT trust.
Outside work he loves watching cricket and following the performances of his son who plays minor counties cricket, as well a charitable work for the local community.
Rupinder Obhi is an experienced primary school teacher with over 20 years of classroom experience. She is a dedicated practitioner committed to supporting pupils’ academic, social, and emotional development. She currently leads Religious Education (RE) and Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education, supporting curriculum development and inclusive practice across the school. Rupinder also has leadership experience at both middle and senior levels and has successfully led the school’s Pupil Parliament, helping to strengthen pupil voice and engagement.
Previously serving as a Staff Governor has given her valuable insight into school governance and the importance of strong collaboration between staff and governors.
Outside of work, Rupinder is a devoted wife and mother of three. She enjoys being creative, going to the gym, spending time with loved ones, and volunteering at her local Gurdwara.
Danielle is a Volunteering Manager at a university, leading the strategic development of programmes that strengthen learner experience, engagement and academic governance. She brings significant experience in governance, representation and community engagement, with a strong track record of leading service development across higher education, charity and legal sectors.
Passionate about widening participation and creating supportive environments, Danielle is motivated by helping individuals navigate complex systems with confidence and is particularly committed to inclusive practice; ensuring processes are fair, transparent and centred on the needs of the individual.
Danielle holds an undergraduate degree in Law and a Level 7 Professional Diploma in Strategic Management and Leadership from the Chartered Management Institute, as well as a Diploma in Professional Marketing.
Danielle built a strong foundation in academic governance and operational leadership throughout her roles within higher education.
Outside of work, Danielle enjoys painting, volunteering in community events and values time spent with family.
Vicky Armer is an experienced Senior Human Resources Business Partner with a strong track record of supporting organisational effectiveness within complex public sector environments. Vicky currently works for Milton Keynes Council, and her team supports Children Services including maintain schools, Public Health, Environment & Property, Planning & Placemaking and Customer Services. Vicky brings significant expertise in workforce planning, organisational change, employee relations, and policy development, working closely with senior leaders to drive sustainable improvement and ensure high-quality service delivery.
Her professional background includes advising on complex staffing matters such as restructures, TUPE transfers, and leadership development, alongside ensuring compliance with employment legislation and best practice. Vicky is recognised for her ability to build trusted relationships, provide balanced and evidence-based advice, and influence decision-making at senior level. She has extensive experience working with stakeholders across multidisciplinary teams, enabling effective collaboration and alignment to share organisational goals.
Vicky holds a degree, post gradual diploma and is a chartered member of the CIPD and committed to continuous professional development, ensuring her knowledge remains up to date with evolving employment law and organisational best practice.
Vicky has governance experience through her involvement with boards, including challenging decision-making and ensuring stakeholders remain aligned. She brings transferable skills and knowledge that would benefit the school and Governing Board.
Vicky is motivated to become a governor to give back to her local community. Having grown up locally and through her work with the local council, she has a strong understanding of the area and is keen to use her experience to support the school and its continued success.
Outside of her professional role, Vicky enjoys maintaining an active lifestyle through regular gym attendance. She has a busy family life with two lively dogs and two teenage children; one has recently completed GCSEs and is preparing to progress to sixth form.
Vicky would bring a thoughtful, pragmatic, and collaborative approach to the governing body, with a clear focus on supporting the Trust’s strategic priorities and ensuring positive outcomes for pupils, staff, and the wider community.

Every school in the East Midlands Academy Trust (EMAT) is committed to providing the highest standard of education so that all pupils are supported to be the best that can be, thought inspiration, inclusion, innovation, integrity and impact. EMAT defines the curriculum as the totality of a child’s experience of education from the Early Years to Post 16, which comprises:
Shepherdswell is a two-form entry infant school in the centre of Milton Keynes, with a social communication department and pre-school onsite. We pride ourselves on being a successful, nurturing and inclusive school at the heart of our community, where we all belong.
The community that we serve is diverse, with our children entering the school from many different ethnic and social backgrounds, 70% of our pupils have English as an additional language, with a diverse range of ethnic groups represented. In the January 2020, 26% of the children had joined the school since the beginning of EYFS. Many in-year admissions occur due to new arrivals to the country or through word of mouth promoting our provision for our social communication department.
At Shepherdswell Academy, 4% of our children have an EHCP with 9% needing SEN support. Our social communication department within school means that we can meet the needs of the individual children with EHCPs, whilst providing the opportunity for them to access mainstream provision where appropriate.
Currently, 24% of children at Shepherdswell are eligible pupil premium funding, 91% of our children fall into the 50% most deprived, in the income deprivation affecting children index (IDACI). As a result of identifying needs within our community, we have additional pastoral members of staff who provide social, emotional and mental health support to our children and their families within the community.
The aim of the curriculum at Shepherdswell Academy is to provide an ambitious, motivating and enriched curriculum that meets the needs of all children, allowing them to explore and understand the world they live in. We provide opportunities for children to develop as independent and confident learners with high aspirations, empowering every child to become a responsible and successful citizen in the local and global community, becoming life-long learners.
Our curriculum incorporates the key knowledge, skills and understanding set out in the National Curriculum and other experiences and opportunities which best meet the learning and developmental needs of the children in our school, equipping them with high levels of literacy and numeracy and critical and creative thinking skills essential for now and in the future. The curriculum is carefully planned with high expectations to ensure clear progression within all curriculum subjects and aims to support children in gaining a deeper understanding of their learning. Our children are provided with a firm grounding in core skills including, reading, writing, spelling, grammar and mathematics.
We recognise the importance of children becoming confident, fluent early readers and fostering a love of books. By establishing an appreciation and love of reading, pupils develop knowledge about themselves and the world in which they live and to gaining access to a broad curriculum. Read Write Inc is well established in school as a systematic approach to teaching phonics and early reading.
We understand the importance of enrichment opportunities and experiences.Children have the opportunity to learn both inside and out of the classroom, including a Forest School, through themed days, whole school activities and opportunities within and out of school which enrich learning. We are a creative school and promote this across the curriculum.A variety of after school clubs based on interests of our children and high-quality visits and visitors extend these opportunities further. Children have opportunities to share their learning with each other, their parents and carers and other learners through school-based performances, competitions and events involving other schools.
We ensure by the time children leave Shepherdswell Academy they are equipped with the knowledge and skills to continue to learn and grow independently in the next stage of their learning journey.

EMAT’s Teaching and Learning Framework
This framework sets out the key principles and theoretical perspectives that inform our curricular thinking across all our schools. It sets out what we believe are important features of the most effective teaching, learning and assessment practices, informed by reliable research. It gives us a ‘shared language’ with which we review, refine and improve our pupils’ educational experiences.
The principles contained within it are not a ‘checklist’, but a conceptual framework that underpins our work to ensure our pupils’ successful learning.

Year 1 Curriculum
Welcome to Year 1
In Year 1 Miss Godfrey is the teacher of Woodpeckers.
The curriculum
Each term we have a topic or theme that we focus our learning around, this term the topic is: into the woods.
We also study a range of books and genres to extend the children’s knowledge and vocabulary. During the year we will have visitors in and visits out of school that enhance and broaden the children’s learning and interests. We will also have opportunities for parents to attend assemblies, workshops, events, and parents’ evenings. Please see the curriculum overview document below.
Reading books
In Year 1 we have a big focus on reading, your child will have a daily phonics lesson and reading for pleasure lesson as well as reading with adults 1:1. In Year 1 we expect your child to read at least 3 times a week for a minimum of ten minutes. Your children will be getting two different types of reading books. One book will be a RWI book that is matched to their phonics/reading ability and the other is a ‘Read with me’ book, your child might not be able to read this book, but it is a great book to share together or even make up different stories using the pictures. Book change days are Monday and Thursdays. Reading at home with your child is extremely important and you should aim to listen to your child read 4 times and record this in their reading record.
PE
For Owls, PE will take place on Wednesday and Thursday. For Woodpeckers, PE will take place on Tuesday and Thursday. On these days, your child should come to school in the correct PE kit. PE can take place both inside and outside, so make sure they are dressed appropriately. Children should have long hair tied up and no earrings on PE days.
Homework
We will have a half termly Homework Pick n Mix. This will be sent out every half term.
General
Please ensure that your child has their named book bag and named water bottle (water only) in school every day and that your child’s uniform is also named. Please check your child’s book bag each day, as letters are often sent this way. The children are provided with a healthy fruit or vegetable snack each morning, these are provided by the government.
If you have any questions please talk to either Ms Whitehead or Miss Godfrey or contact the school office.
We are looking forward to a fantastic year!

Nursery
Shepherdswell Academy Nursery
Our wonderful nursery is organised into morning and afternoon sessions, 5 days a week catering for 2, 3 and 4 year olds. Your child may start at our nursery in the term following their 2nd birthday and stay until they start the Reception year of school.
The Times for Twos project provides funding for up to 15 hours of funded childcare education for eligible two year olds. Children that are 3 are automatically entitled to 15 hours per week childcare funded by the government. We offer these sessions as five morning sessions or 5 afternoon sessions and ask that children are registered with us for 5 days per week.. In addition, we offer a number of 30 hour per week fully funded places, for those eligible and these are subject to availability.
Please check your eligibility at www.gov.uk/apply-free-childcare-if-youre-working
We also accept Tax Free Childcare as payment, for more information please contact the school office.
We offer these sessions as five morning sessions or five afternoon sessions and ask that children are registered with us for five days per week.
The nursery is open term time only. Term dates can be found in the Parents section of our school website.
Currently, in Otters (our provision for three year olds) we offer 26 morning and 26 afternoon places.
Ladybirds, our new provision for two year olds, will offer eight morning and eight afternoon sessions. We are able to increase numbers to 40 across the whole nursery if there is the demand to do so.
